passages.provision_quote: On conviction of an offense under this article, the judge shall enter an order that requires the person to return to the foreign nation from which the person entered or attempted to enter the United States or the person's nation of origin.
passages.note: The engrossed text bundles public-benefit document fraud, SAVE-program verification, lethal-fentanyl sentencing, illegal entry and e-verify false documents in one measure.

rows.reasoning: His only act here is an Aye on HCR2060 (2024), a referral whose own retitling — "border; benefits; fentanyl; illegal entry" — shows it bundles public-benefit fraud, SAVE verification, fentanyl sentencing and e-verify false documents alongside the illegal-entry and return-order sections, so under the vote ladder it shows direction at most. Its return order reaches only people charged under the new state entry offense, and the act states "This section may only be enforced prospectively" for constitutional reasons, which does not say the state should be "leaving long-settled undocumented immigrants in place" nor that it should "Deport all undocumented immigrants, starting with those who have criminal records." No surviving passage matches every clause of one rung, and excluding the other rungs would not establish the one left.
